newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says Britain a low inflation economy.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says Britain a low inflation economy.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday Britain was a low inflation economy regardless of the calculation method used.

Following an announcment from the Office of National Statistics on the rate of British inflation according to European Union harmonised data, Clarke said, "Whatever the measure, whatever the calculation the result is the same -- the UK is now a low inflation economy."
Clarke's comments were delivered in a statement read by a British Treasury official.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) on Wednesday said British consumer prices, when measured on a new harmonised basis with European Union statistics, showed inflation of 2.2 percent in the year to January.

Latest data from the ONS had showed the British retail price index was up 2.8 percent from a year earlier in January. "Core" inflation, which excludes mortgage interest payments, was up 3.1 percent. Both measures were above the government's 2.5 percent target.
Separately, the ONS said Britain had a non-EU trade deficit of 398 million stg in January, down from 640 million stg in December.
On a global basis Britain had a trade deficit of 845 million stg in December, down from 1.037 billion stg in November.
British Treasury Economic Secretary Angela Knight said in a statement, also delivered by a Treasury official, that Britain's trade performance was as strong as it had been for a decade.
"The competitive strength of British industry shines through today's trade figures," she added in the statement.
